name: Bally Ribbon Mills
old_description: Design, development, and manufacturer of specialized engineered woven webbing, tapes, and specialty fabrics.
about:
Bally Ribbon Mills operates from Bally, Pennsylvania, where it has manufactured narrow woven fabrics since 1923. The company began as a specialist in engineered webbing, tapes, and specialty fabrics, and has remained a U.S.-based producer throughout its history.

The firm designs, develops, and weaves a range of products including narrow tapes, webbing, seamless tubular materials, 2-D and 3-D structural shapes, braided structures, and multi-layer composites. Production relies on shuttle looms, needle looms, Jacquard looms, braiding equipment, and specialty broad looms capable of widths up to 72 inches. Post-weave operations cover dyeing, finishing (heat setting, resin treatments, PTFE, silicone, flame retardant), strap cutting, hole punching, sonic welding, and minor sub-assembly. The company states it runs from prototype to full-scale production, though facility size and headcount are not disclosed.

Customers span aerospace, defense, medical, safety, automotive, commercial, and industrial sectors. In aerospace and defense, BRM supplies Mil-Spec webbing and tapes (Mil-W-4088, Mil-DTL-5038K, Mil-W-5625K, Mil-T-87130) that are Berry Amendment compliant. Medical clients receive Class I–III device components such as orthopedic strapping, prosthetic textiles, and dental biotextiles. Safety-market products meet UL and NFPA standards for structural, proximity, and wildland fire-fighting gear.

BRM attributes its position to three factors: a design-engineering team with over 70 years of combined textile experience, including pioneers of 3-D weaving; the ability to weave virtually any yarn—nylon, polyester, aramid, graphite, glass, quartz, ceramic, silicon carbide—into 2-D and 3-D preforms; and a quality system certified to ISO 9001:2015, AS9100D, and ISO 13485:2016 with 24-hour in-house testing.
